1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Within-shift difference-in-differences implemented as a high-frequency event study with repeated on/off treatment episodes, augmented by a visibility-based triple-difference.
- Rationale:
  - The “treatment” is the quasi-exogenous arrival (or departure) of a high-productivity coworker on the same shift. Because managers set schedules based on anticipated demand rather than peer matching, the exact clock-in/clock-out times generate plausibly exogenous within-shift shocks to peer composition.
  - The 10-minute panel permits tight pre/post comparisons around arrivals/departures within the same cashier-shift (cashier × day), absorbing all shift-level shocks (fatigue, baseline demand, promotions, weather).
  - Visibility provides a built-in placebo: the arrival of a high-productivity coworker who is not in the focal cashier’s line of sight should not change the focal cashier’s scanning speed if peer effects operate through observation/social pressure. This enables a robust triple-difference: treated (high-peer visible) vs. placebo (high-peer not visible) vs. low-peer arrivals.
  - To avoid Manski reflection, the treatment is defined using the coworker’s permanent productivity (estimated ex ante), not contemporaneous output.

2. Treatment and Control
- Treatment variable
  - Main: HighPeerVisible_it = 1 if, at time t, at least one coworker with high permanent productivity (e.g., top quartile within store) is on the same shift and in the focal cashier’s visual line of sight.
  - Placebo controls:
    - HighPeerNotVisible_it = 1 if at least one high-productivity coworker is present but not visible.
    - LowPeerVisible_it / LowPeerNotVisible_it analogs using bottom quartile (or bottom 3 quartiles).
  - Alternative continuous exposure: PeerQualityVisible_it = weighted average of permanent productivity of visible coworkers (weights = presence), with analogous NotVisible version.
- Control group (counterfactual)
  - Same cashier, same shift, 10-minute bins when no high-productivity coworker is visible (preferably also no high-productivity coworker present but not visible).
  - Additional counterfactual: windows around arrivals of low-productivity coworkers (placebo).
- Treatment timing / event date
  - Event time is the first 10-minute bin when HighPeerVisible switches from 0 to 1 (arrival) or from 1 to 0 (departure). We implement stacked event windows (e.g., [-60, +60] minutes) around on-switches and off-switches, excluding windows with overlapping additional switches to keep treatment clean in the window.
- RDD (not used): No running variable/cutoff; timing is discrete and pre-scheduled.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
- A1. Exogeneity of within-shift arrival/departure times conditional on fixed effects and controls
  - Clock-in/out times are set by managers ex ante to match anticipated demand, not the focal cashier’s minute-by-minute productivity or peer-matching. With cashier×shift FE and rich time-of-day×store×DOW FE, residual 10-minute shocks are plausibly orthogonal to the exact minute the high peer arrives.
  - Plausibility: High. Scheduling is advance-determined; clock-in minute within a pre-set block is unlikely to respond to focal cashier’s immediate performance.
- A2. No anticipatory adjustment just before the event (local parallel trends)
  - In the hour before a scheduled arrival, focal cashier’s productivity would have followed the same path absent the high-peer arrival (conditional on FE and controls).
  - Plausibility: Testable with event-study leads. Reasonable given limited scope for pre-arrival behavioral change at 10-minute granularity.
- A3. Treatment measured using pre-estimated peer ability avoids reflection
  - We never regress on peers’ contemporaneous output. Using a leave-one-out permanent productivity measure removes simultaneity concerns.
  - Plausibility: High.
- A4. Stable roles and lane assignment within narrow event windows
  - No systematic reassignment of the focal cashier (lane changes, task switches) exactly at peer arrival that would mechanically affect speed.
  - Plausibility: Moderate; we will restrict to windows with stable lane assignment and control for lane FE.
- A5. Limited interference beyond measured peer composition
  - Other coworkers’ arrivals are either controlled for (counts/composition) or windows are chosen to avoid overlapping composition changes.
  - Plausibility: Managed by design via composition controls and window exclusions.

4. Threats to Identification and Remedies
- T1. Demand shocks correlated with scheduled arrivals (e.g., top performers assigned to busier periods within the shift)
  - Remedy:
    - Include very granular time FE: store×day-of-week×10-minute-bin FE (or store×calendar-half-hour×DOW).
    - Cashier×shift (cashier×date×shift) FE to absorb all shift-level shocks (fatigue, promotions, weather).
    - Compare high vs. low coworker arrivals (placebo difference) and visible vs. not-visible (triple-diff). A genuine peer effect should load on visibility and peer quality.
    - Event-study leads to verify flat pre-trends.
- T2. Endogenous lane reassignment or task changes at arrival times
  - Remedy:
    - Control for lane FE; restrict analysis to periods with no lane change in the +/- 60-minute window.
    - Control for the number of open lanes and number of coworkers on shift.
    - Show robustness to excluding first/last 10 minutes of any lane assignment episode.
- T3. Measurement confounds in items-per-second (product mix, coupons, returns)
  - Remedy:
    - Control for lane-by-time fixed effects (if lanes systematically face different product mixes at specific times).
    - Use additional observable controls if available (share of items with coupons, voids/returns). If not available, include store×time-of-day×DOW FE and cashier×shift FE to absorb systematic and idiosyncratic patterns.
    - Re-estimate on baskets with mid-sized item counts where scanning technology dominates.

5. R Code Outline
Note: The code assumes three CSVs:
- panel.csv: 10-minute panel of cashier activity with columns:
  cashier_id, store_id, time_bin (POSIXct), date, dow, tod_bin (0–143), items_scanned, seconds_worked, items_per_sec, lane_id, on_shift (0/1), experience_days, visibility_group (lanes with line-of-sight share group id)
- shifts.csv: cashier_id, date, shift_id, start_time, end_time
- Optional: If visibility is lane-determined, visibility_group is sufficient; otherwise a separate visibility map will be needed.
This code builds peer measures via a self-join, classifies peers by permanent productivity, estimates the main DID with FE, and an event study.

library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(lubridate)

# 1) Load data
panel <- fread("panel.csv")
shifts <- fread("shifts.csv")

# Ensure types
panel[, time_bin := ymd_hms(time_bin)]
panel[, date := as.Date(date)]
panel[, dow := factor(wday(date, label = TRUE))]
panel[, tod_bin := as.integer(tod_bin)]  # 10-min slot 0..143
panel[, store_id := factor(store_id)]
panel[, cashier_id := factor(cashier_id)]
panel[, lane_id := factor(lane_id)]
panel[, visibility_group := factor(visibility_group)]

# 2) Compute permanent productivity (theta) by cashier within store, leave-one-out by week (cross-fitting)
panel[, week := isoweek(date)]
# Overall mean by cashier x store x week
csw <- panel[seconds_worked > 0, .(ips = sum(items_scanned)/sum(seconds_worked)),
             by = .(cashier_id, store_id, week)]
# Out-of-week mean per cashier x store (leave-one-week-out)
setkey(csw, cashier_id, store_id, week)
csw_all <- csw[, .(theta_all = mean(ips, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(cashier_id, store_id)]
csw_merged <- merge(csw, csw_all, by = c("cashier_id","store_id"), all.x = TRUE)
# For simplicity, use theta_all; in production, implement proper out-of-fold means.
theta <- csw_all[, .(cashier_id, store_id, theta = theta_all)]
panel <- merge(panel, theta, by = c("cashier_id","store_id"), all.x = TRUE)

# Classify high/low within store (top quartile = high)
store_quants <- theta[, .(q75 = quantile(theta, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)), by = store_id]
theta <- merge(theta, store_quants, by = "store_id")
theta[, high_peer := as.integer(theta >= q75)]
theta[, low_peer := 1L - high_peer]

# 3) Build within-time coworker composition via self-join
# Keep on-shift rows only
p_on <- panel[on_shift == 1L, .(cashier_id, store_id, time_bin, date, dow, tod_bin,
                                items_per_sec, lane_id, visibility_group,
                                experience_days)]
setkey(p_on, store_id, time_bin)

# Self-join to get coworker rows at same store & time
cow <- p_on[p_on, allow.cartesian = TRUE,
            on = .(store_id, time_bin),
            nomatch = 0,
            suffixes = c("", "_cw")]

# Remove self-pairs
cow <- cow[cashier_id != cashier_id_cw]

# Attach coworker permanent productivity and high/low flags
cow <- merge(cow, theta[, .(cashier_id, store_id, theta_cw = theta,
                            high_peer_cw = high_peer, low_peer_cw = low_peer)],
             by.x = c("cashier_id_cw","store_id"),
             by.y = c("cashier_id","store_id"),
             all.x = TRUE)

# Visibility: visible if same visibility_group
cow[, visible := as.integer(visibility_group == visibility_group_cw)]

# Aggregate to focal cashier-time: counts and indicators
peer_agg <- cow[, .(
  n_cw = .N,
  any_high_vis = as.integer(any(high_peer_cw == 1 & visible == 1)),
  any_high_nvis = as.integer(any(high_peer_cw == 1 & visible == 0)),
  any_low_vis  = as.integer(any(low_peer_cw  == 1 & visible == 1)),
  any_low_nvis = as.integer(any(low_peer_cw  == 1 & visible == 0)),
  avg_theta_vis = ifelse(any(visible == 1),
                         mean(theta_cw[visible == 1], na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_),
  avg_theta_nvis = ifelse(any(visible == 0),
                          mean(theta_cw[visible == 0], na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_)
), by = .(cashier_id, store_id, time_bin)]

# Merge back to panel
panel <- merge(panel, peer_agg, by = c("cashier_id","store_id","time_bin"), all.x = TRUE)
# Replace NAs with 0 for indicator/counts
for (v in c("n_cw","any_high_vis","any_high_nvis","any_low_vis","any_low_nvis")) {
  panel[is.na(get(v)), (v) := 0L]
}

# 4) Fixed effects and controls
# Cashier x shift FE: construct unique cashier_shift_id
shifts[, cashier_id := factor(cashier_id)]
shifts[, shift_id := factor(shift_id)]
panel <- merge(panel, shifts[, .(cashier_id, date, shift_id)], by = c("cashier_id","date"), all.x = TRUE)
panel[, cashier_shift_id := interaction(cashier_id, shift_id, drop = TRUE)]

# Store x time-of-day x DOW FE (10-min bin granularity)
panel[, store_tod_dow := interaction(store_id, tod_bin, dow, drop = TRUE)]

# 5) MAIN SPEC: DID with visibility placebo
# Outcome: items_per_sec. Optionally winsorize at 1/99 to reduce outliers.
panel[, y := items_per_sec]
# Control for number of coworkers on shift (n_cw) to absorb staffing-level changes
# Include lane FE and experience controls (flexible function)
main_mod <- feols(y ~ any_high_vis + any_high_nvis + n_cw + poly(experience_days, 3, raw = TRUE) | 
                    cashier_shift_id + store_tod_dow + lane_id,
                  data = panel[on_shift == 1L],
                  cluster = ~ cashier_id + date)

summary(main_mod)

# 6) EVENT STUDY: arrivals of high-visible peers (on-switches)
# Build treatment indicator and find switches within shift
setorder(panel, cashier_id, date, time_bin)
panel[, treat_hv := any_high_vis]
# Identify on-switches: treat from 0 to 1
panel[, lag_treat := shift(treat_hv, 1L, fill = 0L), by = .(cashier_id, date)]
panel[, on_switch := as.integer(lag_treat == 0L & treat_hv == 1L)]
# Event time index in 10-min bins for a +/- 60 minute window (6 bins either side)
panel[, event_id := NA_integer_]
panel[on_switch == 1L, event_id := .I]  # temporary unique id
# Propagate event_id to window
win <- 6L
panel_es <- panel[!is.na(event_id),
                  .(cashier_id, date, time_bin, event_id)]
# Join around windows
# Create a mapping of all time bins; do a rolling join by time difference
panel[, tnum := as.integer(difftime(time_bin, min(time_bin), units = "mins"))]
eid_map <- panel[on_switch == 1L, .(event_id, cashier_id, date, tnum_event = tnum)]
setkey(panel, cashier_id, date, tnum)
setkey(eid_map, cashier_id, date, tnum_event)
es <- eid_map[panel, allow.cartesian = TRUE, nomatch = 0]
es[, rel := (tnum - tnum_event) / 10]  # in 10-min bins
es <- es[rel >= -win & rel <= win]
# Drop windows with overlapping additional switches within window
overlap <- panel[, .(switch_tnums = list(tnum[on_switch == 1L])), by = .(cashier_id, date)]
es <- merge(es, overlap, by = c("cashier_id","date"))
es[, bad := sapply(switch_tnums, function(v) any(v > (tnum_event - 10*win) & v < (tnum_event + 10*win) & v != tnum_event))]
es <- es[bad == FALSE]
# Merge outcome and controls into es
es <- merge(es, panel[, .(cashier_id, date, tnum, y, any_high_vis, any_high_nvis, n_cw, lane_id, cashier_shift_id, store_tod_dow, experience_days)],
            by = c("cashier_id","date","tnum"), all.x = TRUE)
# Estimate event study with rel dummies, rel = -1 as reference
es[, rel_f := factor(rel)]
es <- es[rel != -1]  # exclude reference
es_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_f, ref = "-1") | cashier_shift_id + store_tod_dow + lane_id,
                data = es,
                cluster = ~ cashier_id + date)
summary(es_mod)
# Plotting coefficients (optional): fixest::iplot(es_mod)

# 7) ROBUSTNESS: Placebo using low-productivity visible arrivals
panel[, treat_lv := any_low_vis]
placebo_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_lv + n_cw + poly(experience_days, 3, raw = TRUE) |
                       cashier_shift_id + store_tod_dow + lane_id,
                     data = panel[on_shift == 1L],
                     cluster = ~ cashier_id + date)
summary(placebo_mod)

# 8) ROBUSTNESS: Visibility triple-difference test
# Test whether coef(any_high_vis) != coef(any_high_nvis)
wald(main_mod, "any_high_vis = any_high_nvis")

# 9) Optional: Continuous exposure to peer quality (visible vs not visible)
cont_mod <- feols(y ~ scale(avg_theta_vis) + scale(avg_theta_nvis) + n_cw + poly(experience_days, 3, raw = TRUE) |
                    cashier_shift_id + store_tod_dow + lane_id,
                  data = panel[on_shift == 1L],
                  cluster = ~ cashier_id + date)
summary(cont_mod)

6. Expected Results
- Direction: Positive peer effects when a high-productivity coworker becomes visible; negligible effects when the same coworker is present but not visible.
- Magnitude: Prior of 1–3% increase in items per second upon high-peer visible arrival (immediate level shift), potentially larger (3–5%) for inexperienced cashiers and in longer exposures. Effects should attenuate when high peers depart.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
- C1: Exogenous within-shift timing of high-peer arrival/departure (conditional on FE/controls): 1
- C2: No anticipatory adjustments in the short pre-window (verified by flat leads): 1 (subject to test)
- C3: No simultaneity/reflection (use of permanent peer productivity only): 1
- C4: No concurrent role/lane changes at event times that mechanically affect speed (addressed by restrictions/FE): 0
- C5: Common trends in short windows / appropriate counterfactual (same cashier-shift + visibility placebo + low-peer placebo): 1

Notes and implementation details
- Compute permanent productivity using leave-one-out or cross-fitting by week to avoid mechanical “own-shift” contamination; the code uses a simple mean for brevity but should be upgraded.
- Consider two-way clustering (cashier and store-date) as specified; alternative is clustering at cashier×store or at shift level.
- Exclude bins with breaks, returns-heavy episodes, or role changes; restrict to stable-lane windows as main sample.
- Report event-study graphs with confidence bands; show no pre-trend and level jumps at arrivals/departures; show larger effects for visibility and for high vs. low peers.
